evidence.excerpt: It is unclear what forward model is used to predict exposure. If the planner uses the true physics simulator ... the system is not circumventing "expensive physical simulation" as implied in the Conclusion. If it uses a learned forward model, it is never defined.

judge_panel.reason: The paper states 'Actions are selected by sampling 200 candidate pulls and choosing the one that maximizes predicted exposure under the estimated state,' but never specifies what forward model is used to predict exposure for each candidate action. The conclusion claims the approach 'can replace expensive physical simulation,' yet if a physics simulator (Laplacian relaxation) is used at planning time to evaluate candidates, this claim is unsupported, and if a learned forward model is used, it is never defined anywhere in the paper.

The paper does specify the planner/environment forward deformation model: "Deformation in response to actions is modeled using a diffusion-based relaxation process [11]" and, in experiments, "Deformation uses Laplacian relaxation [13]." It also states that "Actions are selected by sampling 200 candidate pulls and choosing the one that maximizes predicted exposure under the estimated state," so the claim that the forward model is never defined is factually incorrect.

The reviewer claims the paper fails to specify the forward model used by the planner, but Section II explicitly states: 'Deformation in response to actions is modeled using a diffusion-based relaxation process [11].'
